Parse and print a Cooklang recipe file

Usage: cook recipe read [OPTIONS] [RECIPE]

Arguments:
  [RECIPE]
          Recipe file to read (stdin if not specified)
          
          Can be specified as: - Full path: /path/to/recipe.cook - Relative path: recipes/pasta.cook - Recipe name: "Pasta Carbonara" (searches in recipe directory) - With scaling: recipe.cook:2 or "Pasta:3" (scales by factor) - Stdin: omit to read from standard input
          
          The .cook extension is optional and will be added automatically. When using recipe names (not paths), the tool searches in the current directory and configured recipe directories.

Options:
  -s, --scale <SCALE>
          Scaling factor for ingredient quantities
          
          Multiplies all ingredient quantities by this factor. Can also be specified inline with : syntax (e.g., recipe:2). The inline syntax takes precedence over this flag.
          
          [default: 1]

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v for info, -vv for debug, -vvv for trace)

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          File to write output (stdout if not specified)
          
          The output format can be automatically inferred from the file extension (.json, .yaml, .md, .cook, .tex, .typ, .txt)

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format for the recipe
          
          Available formats: human    - Human-readable text with formatting (default) json     - JSON representation of the recipe data yaml     - YAML representation of the recipe data cooklang - Regenerated Cooklang format markdown - Markdown formatted recipe latex    - LaTeX formatted recipe for creating cookbooks typst    - Typst formatted recipe for creating cookbooks schema   - Schema.org Recipe JSON-LD format
          
          If not specified, format is inferred from output file extension.
          
          [possible values: human, json, yaml, cooklang, markdown, latex, typst, schema]

      --pretty
          Enable pretty formatting for structured output
          
          Adds indentation and formatting to JSON and YAML output. Has no effect on human, cooklang, or markdown formats.

  -p, --paper-size <PAPER_SIZE>
          Paper size for LaTeX and Typst output (default: a4)
          
          Has no effect on other formats.
          
          [possible values: a4, letter, a5, legal]

  -m, --margin <MARGIN>
          Page margin in centimeters for LaTeX and Typst output (default: 2.5)
          
          Applied equally to all four sides. Has no effect on other formats.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
